Rates are in tenths of a percent (75 is 7.5%), so the percentage is `rate / 10`. JavaScript's number-to-string conversion already drops unneeded zeros: 100 gives `10`, 75 gives `7.5`, 50 gives `5`, and 150 gives `15`.

EDIT: app/src/tariff.ts
```
<<<<<<< SEARCH
        lines.push({ label: "Long hire discount", pence: -off });
=======
        lines.push({ label: `Long hire discount (${rate / 10}%)`, pence: -off });
>>>>>>> REPLACE
```

I changed the discount line's label in `quoteHire` to include the percentage, computed as `rate / 10`. The amount, the other lines and the total are untouched. I'm not unsure of anything: all four bands (5, 7.5, 10 and 15) print cleanly with no stray zeros.
